title: Notes on Lighthouses

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Why Lighthouses Flash
paragraphs: Lighthouses flash in distinct patterns so that sailors can tell them apart at night. Each lighthouse has a characteristic, such as one flash every five seconds or two flashes every ten seconds, and these characteristics are printed on nautical charts.

Before electric lamps, lighthouses used oil lamps and later large lenses. The Fresnel lens, made of concentric rings of glass, allowed a relatively small lamp to project a beam visible many kilometres away.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Keepers
paragraphs: Lighthouse keepers maintained the lamp, cleaned the lens and recorded the weather. Most lighthouses have now been automated, and keepers are rarely needed.
